value:
Jacqueline
"Hello out there, my brave soldiers
of the Federation! I hope you're
all well! Jackie here. Doing good
myself, thanks to you all! Now, as
you already know, the Federation's
fight for justice has started here
too, in Australia!"

Jacqueline
"Hello out there, my brave soldiers
of the Federation! I hope you're
all well! Jackie here. Honestly,
I've been going through a rough
patch myself. Thanks to your hard
work, we've got the Zeon Forces on
the ropes, but...ever since the
fighting started, there's been a
lack of food for the civilians.
I've been stuck eating those gross
emergency rations for three whole
days now. Am I doing my part?
Anyway, please, Federation soldiers,
for my sake, take Zeon down
already!"

Maximilian Berger
"Lieutenant Rayer.
Jacqueline's broadcast was canceled
yesterday! I couldn't believe it..."

Anita Julianne
"You're still listening to that
stuff, Mike?! What do you like so
much about that whimsical girl?"

Maximilian Berger
"The fact that she's not jaded like
you are."

Anita Julianne
"What? What did you say, Mike?!"

Maximilian Berger
"Things are getting pretty bad
here, Lieutenant Rayer. At times
like this, I'd relax by listening to
my little flower of the battlefield,
Jacqueline, on the radio, but the
Minovsky particles are interfering
with the reception! This place really
is a hellhole. Sorry, Lieutenant
Rayer. I know how much you were
looking forward to it as well."

Jacqueline
"Hi there, my courageous Federation
soldiers! It's been a while. Jackie
here is doing just fine. I'm sorry I
haven't had a show in such a long
time. I've gotten tons of letters
from all of you, though. I'm so
touched that you were so worried
about me. Listeners had so many nice
things to say about the show, but
one letter made me cry and I'd like
to read it for you.
'My dearest Jacqueline. Before the war
started, I was a member of the
military music band. I was happy
just to give those caught up in
conflict hope and inspiration in
such difficult times. But, after the
war began, I was transferred out,
and now I'm on the front line,
risking my life in dangerous
missions. The first time I came back
after facing real combat, I was so
scared I couldn't sleep at night.
But then I heard your warm, gentle
voice. Even now, it's like a lullaby
for me. Anyway, the missions I'm on
keep getting more and more
dangerous. I don't know when my
insignificant life might meet its
end. So please, please let me hear
your lullaby once more.'
That was a letter from M.
How can they say their life is
insignificant, though?! That's
ridiculous! The war will be over
soon! We're almost there! Please
make it back alive—all of you! As
long as I can keep giving you the
strength to survive, I will keep
singing this lullaby for you!"

Stanley Hawkins
"Rayer, Leung, Mike, Anita... I'm
sorry for asking so much of all of
you. I just have one last selfish
request to ask... Please make it
back alive!"

Anita Julianne
"It looks like the time has come,
Lieutenant Rayer."

Leung Lee-Fai
"This is our final fight,
Lieutenant. Let's give it all we've
got."

Maximilian Berger
"Hey, you're gonna wear yourselves
out. Relax, relax! Lieutenant, let's
go out for some drinks once we
clean things up here!"

Jacqueline
"Brave soldiers of the Federation
Forces and Zeon Forces. Today, the
long-fought conflict between us has
finally ended.

Yesterday, at three o'clock in the
afternoon of January the first,
U.C. 0080, a ceasefire agreement was
signed between the Earth Federation
and the Republic of Zeon. No one
knows how the world may change from
now on, but I believe a day will
come when all of mankind—both
Earthnoids and Spacenoids—will
finally live together in harmony.

So, with the dream of that day in
mind, I'd like to say a prayer for
the souls of all who died in this
war."
